city_center.name: French Quarter (Vieux Carre) + Crescent City Farmers Market
city_center.landmark: French Quarter cast-iron galleries and Jackson Square; Crescent City Farmers Market operating year-round across the city
city_center.notes: Creole river city on the Mississippi. Rouses Markets (Louisiana-founded, Thibodaux HQ) is the dominant home grocer; Winn-Dixie also serves the metro. Crescent City Farmers Market hosts 70+ local farmers, fishers, and food producers. sources: crescentcityfarmersmarket.org; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buildings_and_architecture_of_New_Orleans.

cultural_notes: New Orleans is a Creole city with French, Spanish, Caribbean, and African roots; cafe au lait with chicory and beignets anchor the daily food culture, and the city's calendar turns on Carnival season (source: benjaminmoore.com French Quarter palette; general cultural knowledge; language selection flagged INFERRED)

The French Quarter's most recognizable feature is its cast-iron galleries; despite the French name, the surviving architecture is overwhelmingly Spanish, rebuilt in fire-resistant brick, stucco, and tile after the 1788 and 1794 fires, with Creole townhouses and Caribbean colors (source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buildings_and_architecture_of_New_Orleans; tripshock.com; frenchmarketinn.com)

King cake is the signature Carnival-season food, eaten from Epiphany (January 6) through Mardi Gras, decorated in the purple, green, and gold of Carnival (source: general regional food-culture knowledge)

Creole tomatoes are a short-season Southeast-Louisiana specialty sold at farmers markets and roadside stands from late May through July (source: chefsresource.com Creole tomatoes; nola.com produce guide)
Rouses Markets is a Louisiana-founded grocer (Thibodaux headquarters) and a regional cultural fixture across the Gulf South (source: Rouses regional footprint)
